36	## Local packs — a project's own packs
37	
38	A consumer keeps its **project-specific** packs in its own tree at
39	`.claudinite/local_packs/<name>/` — the same slots (prose `RULES.md`, `rules` checks, `skills`,
40	`run_daily` tasks, `questions`), authored and committed by the project, discovered and run by the
41	same engine as these canon packs. `discoverPacks({ localRoot })` ([registry.mjs](../engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs)) scans this repo's
42	`packs/` **and** the consumer's `local_packs/`; each pack is stamped with its own `dir` (prose and
43	bundled skills resolve off it) and a `local` flag. A local pack:
44	
45	- is **declared by hand** in `.claudinite-checks.json` like any pack — never fingerprinted or seeded
46	  (`detect`/`marker` null) — by its **namespaced token `local_packs/<name>`** (the canonical form;
47	  the engine's [`packEntryId`](../engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs) resolves it and the legacy bare id alike to the bare
48	  pack id, so the bare form keeps working while the fleet's baselining rewrites it), and its id must
49	  be unique (it may not shadow a canon id — the collision is a blocking `config` finding);
50	- **bundles its skills** at `<pack>/skills/<skill>/` (mounted from the tracked pack dir — the
51	  same one shape canon packs use); a bundled skill may carry `checks.mjs`, run when the pack is
52	  active;
53	- rides the deployment plumbing every consumer already vendors: the sync hook preserves
54	  `.claudinite/local_packs/` across its dir swap and the `.gitignore` re-includes it.
55	
56	A local pack contributes **every** slot first-class: prose, checks, skills, **and `run_daily`
57	tasks** — the fleet planner reads a member's local-pack daily descriptors from the member repo by
58	default ([../routines/fleet/local-tasks.mjs](../routines/fleet/local-tasks.mjs)), gated by the
59	member's declaration exactly like a canon pack's tasks. The canon home's own curation tasks ride
60	this path nightly.
61	
62	The canon-vs-local line is the portable-vs-project-specific split ([../extending.md](../extending.md));
63	a project adopts the structure via the `generate-project-instructions` skill, and the growth lifecycle
64	treats `.claudinite/local_packs/` as the project's capture surface.

66	## Settings validity
67	
68	The `"packs"` list and the rest of `.claudinite-checks.json` are validated **when the file loads**, not by a conformance check: [`loadConfig`](../engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs) reports malformed JSON and an unknown top-level property, and the runner adds an unknown *pack name* (it holds the registry). Each becomes a blocking `config` error — a wrong pack name is as much a settings error as invalid JSON. A pack's `detect`/`marker` only **suspects** a pack is wanted; declaring it is the project's call, so a declared pack without its marker (or a marker without its declaration) is **not** flagged.
69	
70	## Pack dependencies (`requires`)
71	
72	A pack states the packs it depends on in an optional `requires` field on its `pack.mjs` — a plain array of pack ids: a release pack builds on its coding pack (`chrome-extension-release` requires `chrome-extension`, `firebase-release` requires `firebase`) and a project-class pack leans on the framework that implements it (`spec-driven-product` requires `executable-requirements`).
73	
74	This is **not a check** — a pack can't be imported without its dependencies, so the resolution happens **when the declaration is written**, at bootstrap `--init` and the baselining backfill ([bootstrap.md](../bootstrap.md) Part 2): [`resolveDeclaredPacks`](../engine/pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs) pulls each declared pack's transitive `requires` closure into `.claudinite-checks.json`. The prerequisite is materialized and visible in the file — droppable like every other entry, the same reason `basics` is written explicitly rather than defaulted — rather than resolved implicitly at run time. Declared ids keep their order; each pack's pulled-in dependencies land right after it.
75	
76	## Bundled skills (`<pack>/skills/`)
77	
78	A pack's skills live in its own tree — `<pack>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`, one owning pack per skill (#385). The directory listing IS the manifest: there is no `skills` field on `pack.mjs` and no separate skills collection to own or cross-declare.
